Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\AtharvaShah\.claude\skills\gtm-toolbelt

# GTM Toolbelt

Each job has exactly one owner among five tools. Zernio publishes. OpenSEO runs SEO for a site. treg buys data. agent-reach reads social
platforms for free. Firecrawl reads and crawls the open web. A workflow can chain them,
but each step has exactly one owner, and the owner is the cheapest tool that passed the
test on 2026-10-03.

## Each Job Has One Owner and One Fallback

| Job | Owner | Cost each | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publish or schedule on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube | zernio | plan | none, never post with another tool |
| Read a known page, crawl or map a site, watch a page for changes | firecrawl | 1 credit a page | agent-reach Jina reader, free |
| Open web search for intent signals (job posts, launches, funding) | agent-reach Exa | free | `firecrawl search`, 2 credits per 10 |
| Read Reddit, X, YouTube transcripts | agent-reach | free | treg: X $0.00075, Reddit $0.0012 |
| Read a LinkedIn member's recent posts | treg `treg.linkedin.user.posts` | $0.0015 | none |
| Find people by company domain and title | treg `treg.people.search` | free | Firecrawl `apollo/people/search`, 0 credits |
| Find a work email | treg `treg.people.email.find` | $0.0048 | Firecrawl `fullenrich/contacts/work-email`, 20 credits |
| Verify an email before you send | treg `treg.people.email.verify` | free | none |
| Enrich a company | treg `treg.companies.enrich` | $0.0018 | Firecrawl `fullenrich/companies/lookup`, 5 credits |
| SEO for a site you own: audits, rank tracking, Search Console, competitors, backlinks, reports | OpenSEO MCP and its 10 skills | credits from the $10 a month plan | treg catalog |
| One-off keyword volume with no site project behind it | treg `treg.google.keywords.volume` | $0.09 a call, up to 1,000 keywords | OpenSEO `get_keyword_metrics` |
| Judge, rank or route any list: lead fit, spam, organic or paid, which offer | Jev, `D:\Atharva\NOTES\SCRIPTS\jev\jev.py` | about $0.00003 a judgement | never Claude reading items one by one |

Two jobs belong to none of the five. Sending an email belongs to Gmail, through the
`gws-gmail` skill, as a draft you approve. Substack DMs and note replies belong to
`NOTES/SCRIPTS/substack/dm.py` and `notes_reply.py`.

## Treg Owns Enrichment Because One Free Firecrawl Account Buys Only 50 Emails

Firecrawl's Alexandria layer resells Apollo, FullEnrich and Data Legion, so both tools sell
the same records. treg won on four counts in the 2026-10-03 test.

1. treg charges $0.0048 for a work email. Firecrawl charges 20 credits for one, and a free
   account gets 1,000 credits a month, so one account buys 50 emails and then stops scraping.
2. Firecrawl refuses every Alexandria call until an org admin accepts the provider's terms,
   once per provider and once per account. You rotate six accounts, so that is up to 18
   acceptances.
3. Firecrawl's free tier allows about 10 requests a minute. The test hit that limit within
   12 requests.
4. treg tries providers cheapest first and charges nothing for a miss on per-success
   endpoints.

Keep Firecrawl's free credits for scraping and crawling, which no other tool here does as well.

treg has one weakness. `treg.companies.enrich` reported PostHog at 29 employees, which is
years out of date. Check headcount against the company's LinkedIn page before you use it
to qualify a lead.

## Agent-Reach Reads Reddit and X for Free Through Your Browser

agent-reach costs nothing because it reads through your own logged-in Chrome session. Exa
search through agent-reach returned five live "founding DevRel" job posts for one query,
and each one is a buyer for a DevRel or content service. `firecrawl search` returned five
blog articles for the same query.

Reddit and X stay dark until you install the OpenCLI Chrome extension and stay logged in
to reddit.com and x.com. Until then, fall back to treg at about $0.001 a call. Firecrawl
refuses Reddit outright.

Never connect agent-reach's LinkedIn channel to your personal account. That channel drives
a logged-in scraper, and LinkedIn restricts accounts that scrape. Your personal profile is
the sales channel, so treg reads LinkedIn for you through providers that use their own
sessions.

## Three Built Pipelines Run the Recipes From treg.to/jev

treg fetches and Jev decides. Three scripts in `D:\Atharva\NOTES\SCRIPTS\gtm` already do this
for atharvashah.com and 10x DevRel, so run them before you build anything by hand. Their
README is the SOP and holds the tested cost of each run.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/gtm/buyer_signal.py devrel      # or: services
python SCRIPTS/gtm/signup_triage.py            # Tally site form and Cal.com bookings
python SCRIPTS/gtm/launch_radar.py --min-faves 50
```

Run them from the vault root. Each script stops at its `--cap` of treg spend.

Every lead hunt keeps only `high` and `qualified` leads, and that rule is Atharva's, not a
default to tune away. A dropped person never reaches a file. The five Jev checks and their
bars live in `TIERS` and `qualify()` in `buyer_signal.py`, and any new hunting script
reuses them.

## Five Workflows Cost Under $1 per 100 Prospects

Every treg call takes a cost cap as a header. Always send one.

```bash
treg call <endpoint> --data '<json>' --header 'X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: 0.02'
```

### W1. Build a Prospect List From Buying Signals

About $0.70 per 100 prospects.

1. Find companies that show a buying signal with free Exa search.
   ```bash
   mcporter call 'exa.web_search_exa(query: "seed-stage devtool hiring founding developer advocate", numResults: 20)'
   ```
2. Find the buyer at each company for free.
   ```bash
   treg call treg.people.search --data '{"company_domain":"posthog.com","title":"marketing","limit":5}'
   ```
3. Find the work email of each person worth contacting, at $0.0048 a hit.
   ```bash
   treg call treg.people.email.find --data '{"full_name":"Jane Doe","domain":"posthog.com"}'
   ```
4. Verify each email for free with `treg.people.email.verify`.
5. Save the list as a CSV in the project you work in. Never paste emails into chat.

The 2026-10-03 hunt for book buyers tested this order on 90 Exa results. It produced 11
qualified buyers for $0.128 of treg spend. Four rules came out of that run.

1. Run keyless Exa at most three calls at a time. A fourth parallel call returns HTTP 429.
2. Use `category:people` in the Exa query to search LinkedIn profiles. A query for
   announcement posts, such as "I joined X as their first developer advocate", finds
   people new in seat. Firecrawl search returned only job ads for the same query.
3. Read each finalist's recent posts with `treg.linkedin.user.posts` before you buy an
   email. Two of ten finalists had left the job that their profile snapshot still showed.
4. Look up email by name plus domain at $0.0048. Lookup by LinkedIn URL costs $0.005 to
   $0.02, so use it only when you do not know the domain.

Firecrawl search with `--tbs qdr:m` beats Exa at one job: finding job posts from the last
month, because keyless Exa has no date filter.

### W2. Warm a LinkedIn Prospect Before the DM

1. Read their last posts for $0.0015 with `treg.linkedin.user.posts` and their profile URL.
2. Comment on one post from your personal account, by hand.
3. Draft the DM from what they posted. You send it, because no tool here touches your
   personal LinkedIn inbox.

### W3. Hunt SEO and AEO Keywords

For a site you work on every week, start in OpenSEO. Run the `seo-project-setup` skill once
per site, then `keyword-research`, `keyword-clustering` and `seo-audit`. OpenSEO keeps the
project context and the Search Console link, so each later session starts informed.

For a one-off check with no project, such as a book title or a post idea, use treg.

1. Put every candidate keyword into one call, because the $0.09 price covers up to 1,000.
   ```bash
   treg call treg.google.keywords.volume --data '{"keywords":["devrel consultant","developer relations agency"],"country":"US"}' --header 'X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: 0.1'
   ```
2. Read what currently ranks with `firecrawl scrape` on the top three URLs.
3. Find SERP and backlink endpoints with `treg catalog search "<job>"`, and read the price
   before you call.

### W4. Listen on Reddit and X for Post Ideas and Reply Targets

1. Search with agent-reach once OpenCLI is connected.
   ```bash
   opencli reddit search "devrel consulting" -f yaml
   twitter search "looking for devrel" -n 20
   ```
2. Without the browser login, use treg at about $0.001 a call:
   `treg.x.search.posts` and `anyapi.reddit.search`.
3. Turn a thread into a post, then publish through W5.

### W5. Publish

Zernio is the only publisher. In the vault, use `python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py` for X and
`python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py` for LinkedIn drafts, and read `SCRIPTS/zernio/README.md`
first. A YouTube video goes through the `youtube-publish` skill (`yt_publish.py`), never through
`post.py`, and the cut must be final before it ships because YouTube cannot replace a video file. From any other repo, the `zernio` MCP server is registered at user scope. A live
send always needs Atharva's explicit yes.

## Check Every Balance Before a Batch

1. Check the treg balance with `treg balance` before a batch. Topping up is Atharva's call
   and his card, so ask him first.
2. Check Firecrawl credits with `firecrawl credit-usage`. When a slot runs out, run
   `python "D:\Atharva\NOTES\SCRIPTS\keys\keys.py" activate`.
3. Check OpenSEO credits with its `whoami` tool, which costs nothing.
4. agent-reach and Exa cost nothing. Reach for them first whenever they cover the job.

## Fund the Balance From the Command Line

The treg web UI does not take the top-up. Use the CLI, and let Atharva type the card.

1. Run `treg topup 10`. It prints a Stripe Checkout link for $10. Atharva opens the link and pays himself. Never type card details for him.
2. Run `treg balance` to confirm. The balance updates in seconds.
3. Set the monthly budget with `treg topup --auto on --threshold 2 --amount 10 --cap 20`. It adds $10 when the balance drops below $2 and never charges more than $20 a month. On 2026-10-03 the account showed auto top-up on with the default cap of $100 a month, so run this command to lower it. Check the result in the `auto top-up` line of `treg balance`.

`--auto on` asks for a typed confirmation and cancels on piped input, so Atharva must run it himself in an interactive terminal. In the Terminal panel on 2026-10-03, `treg` failed with `uv trampoline failed to canonicalize script path`. The same exe works from the Bash tool, so run it in a Git Bash tab.

`treg/SKILL.md` is overwritten by `toolbelt.ps1` on restore, so keep this note here.

## One Script Restores All Five Tools

```powershell
& $HOME\.claude\skills\_config\toolbelt.ps1
```

The script reinstalls all five tools, signs in from `D:\Atharva\NOTES\.env`, registers the
treg, zernio and openseo MCP servers at user scope, and prints the steps only a person can do.
Override the env file with `-EnvFile` or the `CLAUDE_SECRETS_ENV` variable.

## OpenSEO Must Run on the Right Account

On 2026-10-03 the OpenSEO sign-in belonged to marketing@altimate.ai, which is Altimate's
account with 21,302 credits. Use that account only for Altimate sites. Personal SEO for
atharvashah.com, the vault or the DevRel workbench needs `OPENSEO_API_KEY` from a personal
OpenSEO account. Run `whoami` before any paid call to confirm which account is live.

The keyword head-to-head against treg is still open for the same reason. Run the same
five keywords through both once a personal key exists, then fix the one-off row above.

8	
9	# Runtime Contract
10	
11	> **Purpose:** This file says which rules load, in what order, and which checks run at the end.
12	> It is the only file that answers "what was applied to this draft". Read it first, every time.
13	> Adapted from the runtime contract in [Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer](https://github.com/Deupaxx/EveryDay-Writer).
14	> The architecture is theirs. The rules and the voice are mine.
15	
16	## Always loaded
17	
18	Six files load for every piece of writing, on every channel, in this order.
19	
20	1. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`, this file. The load order and the checks.
21	2. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md`. The failure patterns a regex cannot see.
22	3. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/write-simply.md`. The plain style, and the test for whether the ideas are right.
23	4. `DIGITAL TWIN/World.md`. The villain, the vision, and what the piece is for.
24	5. `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`. The bar the insight clears before a word is drafted.
25	6. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`. How the writing sounds.
26	
27	Files 2 and 3 are a pair. The pattern rules say what to remove, and `write-simply.md` says what to
28	aim for, so a draft that only obeys the first one reads stripped.
29	
30	`World.md` decides what the piece argues and `Voice.md` decides how it sounds, so the two never
31	collide. Name the skill-tree node before you draft a line. A piece that advances no node is an
32	idea, so send it back to `SUBSTACK/0_IDEAS/`.
33	
34	`net-new-value.md` is the guiding principle for all content, on every channel. Write the core
35	insight as one sentence and name its box before you draft. Only box 4 ships: non-obvious to the
36	reader and tactical enough to use today. A piece outside box 4 gets one upgrade, then goes back to
37	the idea bank.
38	
39	`SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` holds the banned words, phrases and punctuation. `DIGITAL TWIN/rules/`
40	holds the prose rules, one file each. The `core` rules load into every session through the generated
41	block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so you never copy them into another file.
42	
43	The `craft` rules load for every writing job. Run this once per session before the first draft:
44	
45	```bash
46	python SCRIPTS/slop/rules_prompt.py --profile craft
47	```
48	
49	## Loaded on demand
50	
51	One more file loads, chosen by the job. Never load two.
52	
53	| The job | Load this |
54	|---|---|
55	| A Substack article, an essay, a long piece | `DIGITAL TWIN/Long-Form Writing Rules.md` |
56	| A tutorial, a how-to, a README, developer docs | `DIGITAL TWIN/Technical Writing Style Guide.md` |
57	| A LinkedIn post, a Note, a tweet, a caption | nothing extra. The channel skill carries it |
58	
59	`DIGITAL TWIN/AI Writing Policy.md` outranks all of the above and it changes rarely, so read it
60	when you start a writing session and not once per draft.
61	
62	## Then the channel skill
63	
64	The skill carries the shape of the channel and nothing else. It never restates a banned word, a
65	voice rule or a craft rule, because a copy goes stale and then two files disagree.
66	
67	| Channel | Skill |
68	|---|---|
69	| LinkedIn post | `.claude/skills/write-linkedin-posts/SKILL.md` |
70	| X post or thread | `.claude/skills/banger-tweets/SKILL.md` |
71	| Substack Note | `.claude/skills/substack-notes/SKILL.md` |
72	| Substack article | `.claude/skills/substack-writer/SKILL.md` |
73	| Reddit post | none. `SOCIALS/Reddit/README.md` is the channel spec |
74	| Landing page or sales email | `.claude/skills/write-sales-copy/SKILL.md` |
75	| A stuck idea with no shape yet | `.claude/skills/write-outline/SKILL.md` |
76	| An existing draft that reads like AI | `.claude/skills/deslop-audit/SKILL.md` |
77	
78	## Precedence, higher wins
79	
80	Four layers can disagree. Resolve upward.
81	
82	1. The banned lists in `slop_rules.py` and the patterns in `core/pattern-rules.md`.
83	2. The channel skill.
84	3. `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`.
85	4. A sample Atharva pastes in the current session.
86	
87	A sample beats the profile. The profile beats the skill. Two rules never override anything above
88	them. The fabrication rule below, and the five principles in `AI Writing Policy.md`.
89	
90	## The fabrication rule
91	
92	Add no fact that Atharva did not supply. That covers a name, a number, a date, a statistic, a
93	quote, a source, an event and a client. This rule bites hardest on a rewrite, because the fix for
94	a vague sentence looks like a specific sentence, and the specifics are not yours to invent.
95	
96	You have three legal moves when a sentence needs a real detail.
97	
98	1. Ask him for it.
99	2. Mark the gap in visible brackets, such as `[the real number]`. Brackets cannot ship by accident.
100	3. Drop the claim to the level the evidence supports, or cut it.
101	
102	An invented specific that reads well is a worse defect than the vague sentence it replaced. A
103	reader cannot catch it.
104	
105	## The two-pass loop
106	
107	Never hand over a first draft.
108	
109	**Pass 1.** Write it. Do not judge while you write.
110	
111	**Pass 2.** Read it cold and answer five questions for yourself, in writing. Do not print the
112	answers unless he asks.
113	
114	1. If a reader called this AI, which exact sentence would they point at?
115	2. Does the draft carry a fact, a name, a number or a source that he did not give me?
116	3. Which sentence is the weakest, and does the piece rest on it?
117	4. Which sentence reads worst, and is the idea under it wrong rather than the wording?
118	5. Is the core insight still box 4 in `core/net-new-value.md`, or did the draft sand it down to box 2?
119	
120	**Pass 3.** Fix what the answers found. Then run the checks.
121	
122	## Announce the load order
123	
124	Render this panel above every draft. Do not type it by hand.
125	
126	```bash
127	python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py --skill <channel skill> --file "<path>"     --node "<the skill-tree node this piece advances>"     --topic "<the idea, for the pillar check>"     --season "<NN beat N, or none>" --format "<number and name, or n/a>"     --insight "<the box 4 insight, one sentence>"
128	```
129	
130	`--glob "<pattern>"` replaces `--file` for a batch, and reports the worst result
131	across the set. `--plain` drops to ASCII. `--technical` swaps the on-demand file
132	for the Technical Writing Style Guide. The script exits 1 when any measured check
133	failed, so a caller can gate on it.
134	
135	```
136	╭─ LOAD ORDER ─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
137	│ ✓ 1  core/runtime-contract              always               │
138	│ ✓ 2  core/pattern-rules                 always               │
139	│ ✓ 3  core/write-simply                  always               │
140	│ ✓ 4  World.md                           always               │
141	│ ✓ 5  core/net-new-value                 always               │
142	│ ✓ 6  Voice.md                           always               │
143	│ ✓ 7  Long-Form Writing Rules.md         on demand            │
144	│ ✓ 8  skill:substack-writer              channel              │
145	├─ WORLD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
146	│ villain  rented work                                         │
147	│ node     builds a gate that refuses bad work                 │
148	│ season   01 beat 3      format  05 Contrarian Take           │
149	│ insight  a hook that returns decision: block stops the save  │
150	├─ CHECKS, measured ───────────────────────────────────────────┤
151	│ ✓ pillar      ON (AI)                                        │
152	│ ✓ slop        CRIT 0                                         │
153	│ ✓ clarity     CRIT 0                                         │
154	│ ✓ craft       0                                              │
155	│ ✓ seo         CRIT 0                                         │
156	╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
157	```
158	
159	The two halves carry different weight, and the difference is the point.
160	
161	**The top half is declared.** You state the node, the season and the box 4 insight. The chain itself
162	comes from the channel table inside the script, so it cannot drift from this file.
163	
164	**The bottom half is measured.** The script runs each scorer and prints what it
165	returned. A tick means a check ran and passed. A cross means it ran and failed. A
166	dot means the scorer could not run, which never reads as a pass.
167	
168	That split is why the panel replaced the four hand-typed lines it used to be. A
169	typed line could claim `slop CRIT 0` for a check nobody ran, which is the blind
170	spot this contract exists to close. A rendered line cannot.
171	
172	A missing panel means the chain was skipped.
173	
174	## The checks, in this order
175	
176	Run them in order. A later check on a draft that fails an earlier one wastes both your time and his.
177	
178	| Order | Command | Bar |
179	|---|---|---|
180	| 0 | Name the box in `core/net-new-value.md` for the one-sentence insight | Box 4. Every channel |
181	| 0b | The opening gate in `LIBRARY/Resources/Post Uniqueness Check.md` | The top-ranked of 5 openings ships, and no hook is a question. LinkedIn, X, Notes |
182	| 1 | `python SCRIPTS/pillars/pillars.py --text "<the idea>"` | ON, or an honest BEND |
183	| 2 | `python SCRIPTS/substack/overlap.py check "<the idea>"` | WRITE. Articles only |
184	| 3 | `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0 |
185	| 4 | `python SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0. Every channel |
186	| 5 | `python SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py "<file>"` | CRIT reaches 0. LinkedIn only |
187	| 6 | `python SCRIPTS/substack/craft.py "<file>"` | 0. Articles only |
188	| 7 | `python SCRIPTS/seo/score.py "<file>" --write` | 0. Articles only |
189	| 8 | `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py` | no `source_blog` warning. Social files only |
190	| 9 | `python SCRIPTS/review/build.py` | the desk carries it. Every draft is on it, nothing to stamp |
191	
192	Rows 4, 5 and 6 were missing from this table until 2026-09-04. All three existed
193	and two of them already blocked a commit, so the table was the only place that
194	disagreed. A check absent from this file gets skipped by anyone who trusts it,
195	which is the whole reason the file exists. Add a row here in the same commit
196	that adds a scorer.

199	so, and say in the announcement block which rows you skipped.
200	
201	MED and LOW findings from the scorer are advisory. On short-form, ignore its flow, paragraph and
202	fragment findings, because those rules were written for long-form.
203

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\AtharvaShah\.claude\skills\social-cards

# Social Cards

Atharva reviewed 99 of these on 2026-09-27 and called them his real edge. That batch is the
bar. A new card matches it or beats it, and the 14 cards in `examples/` show what that means.

The whole method fits in one sentence. **Real material, one focal idea, layered like a
thumbnail designer would, checked at phone size before it ships.** Everything below is how.

## A YouTube Thumbnail Is Not a Card

For a 1280x720 YouTube thumbnail, skip the four layers, Anton caps and stickers below. Read
`references/youtube-thumbnails.md` and start from `examples/yt-ask-bookshelf/`, rendered with
`kit/render_yt.py`. The rule: one benefit line, one real query or object, the real result, nothing
else. A heavy-stroke yellow Anton thumbnail was rejected as "old fashioned" on 2026-10-05.

## Four Layers Make a Card Look Designed Instead of Drawn

Every card is a 1080x1350 HTML page (4:5) with four stacked layers, rendered at device scale 2
to a 2160x2700 PNG and a JPG for upload.

1. **Background layer.** A real photo or a real screenshot, color graded, blurred when it sits
   behind type. A wall of real items tilted in 3D perspective is the strongest version
   (`examples/211-covers`, `examples/substack-cli-own-the-pipe-125-images`).
2. **Hero layer.** The one object the post is about: a terminal with genuine output, a live
   page screenshot on a tilted card, a receipt, a document, a cutout of a person.
3. **Type layer.** A headline of 7 words or fewer, at least 90 px tall, usually Anton in caps.
   The post's biggest number goes here when it has one, at 250 to 330 px.
4. **Accent layer.** At most one sticker, one marker circle or strike, one hand-written arrow.
   Then `.vignette` and `.grain` from the kit on every card, because film grain is the single
   biggest signal that separates a designed image from a flat vector.

The kit's byline (avatar plus "Atharva Shah · blog.atharvashah.com") sits bottom left on every
card. It is the brand mark that makes a feed of these read as one author.

## Real Material Beats Drawn Material Every Time

The cards that landed hardest all used something real. Reach for material in this order.

1. **A real screenshot of the real thing.** Render the live page with Playwright at 2x. GitHub
   repo headers, docs pages, a search result, a pricing page, a support article with the key
   sentence circled (`examples/google-indexing-tools-twice`, `examples/kubearmor-bottom-up`).
2. **Genuine output.** Run the actual command and paint its real text into a terminal window.
   `git grep` results, scorer output, `curl` responses, `git show` diffs
   (`examples/never-type-a-count-into-copy`, `examples/fabricated-testimonials-deleted`).
3. **His own assets.** `META/Attachments/**`, `SUBSTACK/_COVERS/*.png`, BRAG_LIST.md, the vault
   files themselves, his site pages.
4. **A free-license photo.** Wikimedia Commons (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA), Unsplash, Pexels. A
   CC BY or CC BY-SA photo carries a 15 px credit line bottom right: "Photo: author, license,
   via site". Get the author from the Wikimedia API
   (`action=query&prop=imageinfo&iiprop=extmetadata`).

A generic stock photo of business people, a flat icon grid, clip art, and an image model are
all out. The card is composited, never generated.

## Twelve Concepts Cover Almost Every Post

Pick the concept from the post's strongest fact, then give it a palette no neighbour in the
batch uses. Full breakdowns with the CSS moves are in `references/concepts.md`.

| Concept | When the post has | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Giant number over proof | One big figure | `meeting-transcripts`, `kubearmor-bottom-up` |
| Wall of real items in 3D | Many of one thing | `211-covers`, `substack-cli-own-the-pipe-125-images` |
| Receipt | Prices or a cost stack | `saas-stack-460-a-month` |
| Struck wrong, circled right | A correction | `never-type-a-count-into-copy`, `brand-orange-fails-contrast` |
| Terminal with genuine output | A command or a script | `fabricated-testimonials-deleted` |
| Two windows, same page | A duplicate or a contrast | `google-indexing-tools-twice` |
| Versus bars drawn to scale | Two durations or sizes | `ai-video-trust-gap` |
| Fanned live screenshots | A list of tools or sites | `three-references-one-direction` |
| Numbered build bands | Steps in order | `ai-security-ctf-one-day` |
| Person cutout plus claim | A named person's method | `packaging-limited-content` |
| Photo with a cut stat bar | A share of people | `zappos-deleted-every-title` |
| Official doc, sentence circled | "The source already says this" | the watermark card in the vault |

## Nine Rules Stop a Card From Shipping

1. Every word and number on the card comes from the post. When the source disagrees with the
   post, keep the number off the card and report the mismatch. Never invent a figure.
2. No fake UI that claims to show something that did not happen. Real output only.
3. Blur the names of private people in any screenshot. A real person shown by face needs a
   reason in the post, and the report names it for review.
4. Company logos appear only when the post names that company.
5. No em dash or en dash in on-card text, and no emoji on the card.
6. Nothing but the byline in the bottom 140 px. Stickers collided with it twice.
7. Text never sits on a busy area without a fade, a panel or a stroke.
8. Use `kit/face-clean.png` for Atharva's face, never the raw cutout, which carries a blue
   fringe. Use it on at most one card in five, and only where a human reaction helps.
9. Carousel PDFs from old folders are not trusted. They carried em dashes, stale numbers and
   unsourced quotes every time. Post the card as a single image unless the carousel was
   checked in this session.

## Make One Card in Six Steps

1. Read the whole post, including frontmatter. A `visual:` field is Atharva's planned shot, so
   start there. Write the post's strongest fact in one line.
2. Scaffold the folder:
   `python ~/.claude/skills/social-cards/kit/new_card.py <cards_root> <slug> --size linkedin`.
   In the vault, `<cards_root>` is `META/Attachments/li-images`.
3. Gather the real material into `<slug>/assets/`. Screenshots with Playwright at
   `device_scale_factor=2`. Downloads with the Git-bundled curl
   (`"/c/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/curl.exe" -sL -o <file> <url>`), because this machine's
   Python has an expired CA root.
4. Build `card.html` on the kit classes: `.display`, `.heavy`, `.mono`, `.serif`, `.marker`,
   `.pop`, `.glow`, `.hl`, `.shot`, `.sticker`, `.byline`, `.grain`, `.vignette`. The CSS moves
   that do the most work are in `references/techniques.md`.
5. Render: `python <cards_root>/_kit/render.py <cards_root>/<slug>/card.html`. Run it from the
   repo root. In the vault, never `cd` first, because the vault hooks use relative paths.
6. Read `_preview-540.jpg` with the Read tool. That is the size a phone shows. Fix what you
   would not ship and render again. Two passes minimum. Then write `meta.json`:
   `{"slug", "post", "alt", "sources"}`, where `alt` says what the image shows in 250
   characters or fewer.

## Batches Run as Parallel Agents of Five

For more than 5 cards, split the posts into groups of 5 and give each group to one background
agent. The playbook for the orchestrator, including the brief to paste, the contact-sheet QA
and the ship step, is `references/pipeline.md`. The short version:

- Finish one reference card yourself first, and point every agent at it and at `examples/`.
- One agent owns one set of slug folders and writes nothing else. Each agent keeps its scratch
  files inside its own slug folder, because a shared scratchpad got overwritten twice.
- Review the batch as a contact sheet, never card by card:
  `magick montage <dir>/{a,b,c,d,e}/_preview-540.jpg -tile 5x1 -geometry 360x450+6+6 -background '#222' sheet.jpg`.
- Collect every source mismatch the agents report into one list for Atharva. In the first
  batch, 29 of 99 posts carried a number or a claim that disagreed with its own source.

## LinkedIn Posts Get Wired and Pushed After the Card

Inside the vault, a finished card is wired into its post and pushed as a Zernio draft.

1. `python META/Attachments/li-images/_kit/groom.py <slug> ...` sets `media_asset:` and
   `media_alt:` in the post and gives the pinned comment its blog and book-a-call lines.
2. Run `SCRIPTS/slop/score.py`, `SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py` and `SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py`.
   All three reach CRIT 0.
3. `python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py <post files>` dry-runs. `--live` saves drafts on the
   personal LinkedIn profile with the image, the alt text and the first comment. It refuses the
   AccuKnox page, and a drafted post never publishes by itself.
4. `python SCRIPTS/review/build.py` so the desk shows the image.

Zernio deletes uploaded media after 7 days, so a draft needs posting or a re-push inside a week.

## Other Platforms Change the Canvas, Never the Method

`render.py --size` takes `linkedin` and `instagram` (1080x1350), `x` (1080x1350, full height
on the mobile timeline), `x-wide` (1600x900), `square` (1080x1080) and `substack-inline`
(1456x816). A Substack hero cover still comes from `SUBSTACK/_COVER-ENGINE/`, which owns that
format. An X post carries no link, so the card must carry the whole idea on its own.

The evidence behind the 4:5 canvas and the first-comment links is in
`D:\Atharva\NOTES\LIBRARY\Resources\LinkedIn Feed Ranking 2026 - 360Brew.md`.
